nodes.name: NiFe LDH-CA2 hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: NiFe LDH-CA2 (sodium citrate content 0.14 mmol) was prepared with a simple hydrothermal method: 1.28 mmol nickel nitrate hexahydrate, 0.22 mmol iron sulfate, 8.3 mmol urea, and 0.14 mmol sodium citrate were mixed in 20 mL pure water. After stirring for 30 min, the transparent solution was placed into a Teflon-lined autoclave. The cleaned nickel foam (NF) was soaked into solution at 120 °C for 8 h. After cooling naturally, the pieces were washed with ethanol and water several times. Then, these pieces were dried at 60 °C for 4 h.

nodes.name: Pure Ni(OH)2-CA2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: The pure Ni(OH)2·CA2 was similarly prepared with 0.14 mmol sodium citrate using the same hydrothermal method as NiFe LDH-CA2 but using only nickel nitrate hexahydrate source without iron sulfate: nickel nitrate hexahydrate, 8.3 mmol urea, and 0.14 mmol sodium citrate mixed in 20 mL pure water (proportions adjusted for single metal). After stirring for 30 min, the transparent solution was placed into a Teflon-lined autoclave. The cleaned nickel foam (NF) was soaked into solution at 120 °C for 8 h. After cooling naturally, the pieces were washed with ethanol and water several times. Then, these pieces were dried at 60 °C for 4 h.
nodes.source_text: The pure Ni(OH)2·CA2 and Fe(OH)3–CA2 were similarly prepared with 0.14 mmol sodium citrate.

nodes.name: Pure Fe(OH)3-CA2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: The pure Fe(OH)3–CA2 was similarly prepared with 0.14 mmol sodium citrate using the same hydrothermal method as NiFe LDH-CA2 but using only iron sulfate source without nickel nitrate hexahydrate: iron sulfate, 8.3 mmol urea, and 0.14 mmol sodium citrate mixed in 20 mL pure water (proportions adjusted for single metal). After stirring for 30 min, the transparent solution was placed into a Teflon-lined autoclave. The cleaned nickel foam (NF) was soaked into solution at 120 °C for 8 h. After cooling naturally, the pieces were washed with ethanol and water several times. Then, these pieces were dried at 60 °C for 4 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Bragg diffraction peaks match typical NiFe LDHs (JCPDS no. 40-0215) with slight peak shifts of (003) and (006) planes indicating enlarged interlayer spacing from 7.8 Å for NiFe LDH to 7.9 Å for NiFe LDH-CAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of pre-catalysts are exhibited in Fig. 1. Bragg diffraction peaks of these pre-catalysts match well with typical NiFe LDHs (JCPDS no. 40-0215)... the calculated interlayer spacing increases from 7.8 Å for NiFe LDH to 7.9 Å for NiFe LDH-CAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-CA2 shows mesoporous structure constructed of ultrathin nanosheets uniformly distributed on Ni foam, denser than NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the SEM images (Fig. 2(a) and (b)), we can see that NiFe LDH-CA2 has a mesoporous structure constructed of ultrathin nanosheets uniformly distributed on Ni foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-CA2 shows ultrathin nanosheet structure with coexistence of crystalline (lattice spacing 2.0 Å, (018) facet) and disordered regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images of NiFe LDH-CA2 are shown in Fig. 2(g)–(i). The ultrathin nanosheet structure is observed... A lattice spacing of around 2.0 Å can be obtained in the crystal region, which is indexed to the (018) facet.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms coexistence of crystals and disordered structure in NiFe LDH-CA2 with lattice spacing of 2.0 Å indexed to (018) facet of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (see in Fig. 2(i)) shows the coexistence of crystals... and indexed to the (018) facet in a typical NiFe LDH (JCPDS no. 40-0215).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping of NiFe LDH-CA2 shows C, O, Ni, and Fe elements homogeneously distributed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping images of NiFe LDH-CA2 (Fig. 2(c)–(f)) show that C, O, Ni, and Fe elements are homogeneously distributed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Type-H3 hysteresis loops confirm mesoporous structure with specific surface areas of 38.4 m²/g (NiFe LDH), 74.2 m²/g (CA1), 81.1 m²/g (CA2), 44.2 m²/g (CA3); pore sizes mainly 3-4 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This is supported by BET measurements: the N₂ adsorption/desorption isotherms... Specific surface areas of 38.4 m² g⁻¹ for NiFe LDH, 74.2 m² g⁻¹ for NiFe LDH-CA1, 81.1 m² g⁻¹ for NiFe LDH-CA2, and 44.2 m² g⁻¹ for NiFe LDH-CA3 were obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: New bands at 909 and 1072 cm⁻¹ (C-H bending, C-O stretching) and intensified 1389/1620 cm⁻¹ (COO⁻ stretching) confirm CA intercalation in NiFe LDH-CAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the intercalation of CA, new bands at 909 and 1072 cm⁻¹, originating from C–H bending and C–O stretching, can be obtained, indicating the existence of CA in NiFe LDH-CAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman bands shift from 454/538 cm⁻¹ to 443/521 cm⁻¹ with CA intercalation; new peaks at 1570 cm⁻¹ (C=O) and 2920 cm⁻¹ (-CH₂-) confirm citrate presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the intercalation of CA, the Raman bands possess a negative shift to 443 cm⁻¹ and 521 cm⁻¹... new Raman peaks at 1570 and 2920 cm⁻¹ indexed to the vibration of C=O and stretching of -CH₂- in citrate anions.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-CA2 shows Ni 2p peaks at 873.7/856.0 eV (Ni²⁺), 874.8/857.1 eV (Ni³⁺) with Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ ratio 1.81; Fe 2p peaks at 713.0/725.7 eV (Fe³⁺) shifted +0.2 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spectra can be separated into characteristic peaks located at 873.7, 856.0, 874.8, and 857.1 eV... The ratio of Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ is raised from 1.10 to 1.81 with CA intercalation.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH-CA2 shows double layer capacitance Cdl = 2.06 mF cm⁻² indicating highest ECSA among tested catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be seen that NiFe LDH-CA2 possesses larger Cdl (2.06 mF cm⁻²) than other electrocatalysts (0.81 mF cm⁻² for NiFe LDH, 1.56 mF cm⁻² for NiFe LDH-CA1, and 1.64 mF cm⁻² for NiFe LDH-CA3), proving the higher ECSA and more active cites for OER promotion.
